texts.preamble: James M.J. @ Chacko vs Cherupuzha Grama Panchayath Committee on 26 September, 2018 Author: Shaji P.Chaly Bench: Shaji P.Chaly In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam Present The Honourable Mr. Justice Shaji P.Chaly Wednesday, The 26Th Day Of September 2018 / 4Th Aswina, 1940 WP(C).No. 18726 of 2018 Petitioner/S: 1 James M.J. @ Chacko, Aged 66 Years, S/O.Chacko, Moongamackal House, Kakkayanchal, Cherupuzha P.O., Kannur District. 2 Chinnamma James, Aged 64 Years, W/O.James, Moongamackal House, Kakkayanchal, Cherupuzha P.O., Kannur District. texts.facts: This writ petition is filed by the petitioners seeking to quash Ext.P43 decision of the Committee of the 1st respondent, whereby the renewal of licences sought for by the petitioners is declined by the Panchayat. Material facts for the disposal of the writ petition are as follows: 2. First petitioner was granted licence for manufacturing packaged drinking water, and for its sales by the respondent Panchayat, during 2014, and is conducting the business in the name and style of 'Goodly Enterprises', Kozhichal, which is situated in Ward No.10 of 1st respondent Panchayat and conducted in Building No.CP 10/154-B. 3. The 2nd petitioner was granted licence for manufacturing and sale of Soda and Soft Drinks by the respondent Panchayat from 2014 onwards, and is functioning under the name and style 'Grace Enterprises', Kozhichal, situated in the very same Ward and Building bearing No.CP 10/154-A, adjacent to the 1st petitioner's unit. According to the petitioners, they have, all the required licences and clearances from the concerned Departments and had been doing the business without violating any of the conditions laid down by the concerned Departments. 4. The 2nd respondent issued an order to stop the business, alleging that, they are extracting water unauthorizedly and the local people is protesting. Challenging the above specified orders, petitioners have approached this Court by filing W.P.(C) No.10883 of 2017, and has secured Ext.P21 judgment, wherein certain directions were issued, and till such time, petitioners were permitted to operate the units. However, according to the petitioners, thereafter, petitioners were threatened with demolition of the alleged unauthorized constructions, and thereupon, petitioners approached this Court by filing W.P.(C) No.16914 of 2017 and has secured Ext.P28 judgment, wherein the Panchayat was directed to consider the applications for James M.J. @ Chacko vs Cherupuzha Grama Panchayath Committee on 26 September, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70803976/ 2 renewal of the licences within one month from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment. 5. According to the petitioners, the 2nd respondent has declined the renewal as per Ext.P29 order. Thereupon, petitioners were constrained to approach this Court by filing W.P.(C) No.6027 of 2018 and has secured Ext.P31 judgment, wherein the 1st respondent Panchayat was directed to consider along with a direction to ensure that the petitioners close down a bore well situated in the property and also directed the Panchayat to take a fresh decision in the licence applications submitted by the petitioners. According to the petitioners, in accordance with the directions issued by this Court in Ext.P31 judgment, the bore well was closed down, however, despite the same, the Panchayat has declined the licence as per Ext.P43. Petitioners have also produced Ext.P41 series of photographs to show that the bore well is closed, as directed in Ext.P31 judgment. These are the background facts projected by the petitioners to secure the reliefs sought for in the writ petition. 6. The 1st and 2nd respondents have filed a detailed counter affidavit, refuting the allegations and claims and demands raised by the petitioners. Among other contentions, it is stated that, as per Ext.P31 judgment, this Court directed the 1st respondent Panchayat to consider the application submitted by the petitioners for renewal of licence afresh, in accordance with law, and it was also directed that the directions contained in Ext.P28 shall also be complied with and the units shall be operated only in strict compliance with the conditions imposed by the local authority. It is the further case of the respondents that, since the petitioners have not complied with all the necessary requirements, Ext.P43 order was passed, on the basis of the local inspection conducted by the officers of the Panchayat and they were satisfied that the water level has increased after the working of the petitioners units were stopped. 7. That apart, it is submitted that, Ext.P43 order passed by the Committee of the 1st respondent is an appealable order as per Sec.276(5) of the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994. As per Ext.P21, this Court directed to submit objections to Exts.P16 and P17 stop memos and the Secretary of the Panchayat was directed to consider the same in accordance with law. On the basis of the said directions, Ext.P22 objection was submitted and the Panchayat has passed Exts.P23 and P24 orders dated 19.04.2017. The renewal of licences was declined stating that the petitioners have carried out James M.J. @ Chacko vs Cherupuzha Grama Panchayath Committee on 26 September, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70803976/ 3 construction of an additional bore well without securing permission from the Panchayat, and also that petitioners carried out modification of the existing building without securing permit from the Panchayat. That apart, it is stated that, petitioners are drawing more water than permitted. Ext.P26 is the minutes of the meeting of the Panchayat Committee. 10. Anyhow, being aggrieved by Exts.P23 and P24 and the decision of the Panchayat Committee, petitioners have preferred a writ petition and has secured Ext.P28 judgment, wherein the Panchayat Committee was directed to re-consider the requests made by the petitioners, in view of the withdrawal of the earlier decision of the Committee. On the said basis, directions were issued as to the manner in which the application submitted by the petitioners is to be considered. Thereupon, the Panchayat Committee has taken Ext.P30 decision wherein the Committee has taken the decision that since there is acute water shortage in the said area, the licences of the petitioners need not be renewed. It was also found therein that, the electricity bills paid by the petitioners will show that petitioners are drawing water from the bore well more than the quantity prescribed to them by the Pollution Control Board. However, the said order was again challenged and Ext.P31 judgment was rendered by this Court, wherein it is recorded that, on the petitioners making a request for the presence of the officials of the Panchayat for witnessing the closing of the second bore well, necessary steps shall be taken, and also to comply with the directions contained in Ext.P29 judgment, which directions were rendered on the basis of the submission made by the Secretary of the Panchayat that the Panchayat has no objection in taking a fresh decision.
texts.arguments: Further, it is pointed out that, Ext.R1(a) notice was issued, pointing out that the construction carried out by the petitioners is illegal. It is also stated that, the petitioners are not carrying on the business in accordance with law. So also, it is submitted that, the Panchayat is duty bound to protect and maintain the traditional drinking water sources, and there is depletion of water and petitioners are drawing more water than that is permitted by the Pollution Control Board in its consent orders. 11. It was thereupon that, Ext.P43 order is now passed by the Panchayat, refusing licences, basically for the reason that there is acute water shortage in the area and the petitioners are drawing water in excess of the quantities prescribed to them and also that, as is undertaken in Ext.P31 judgment, the bore well is not closed. Further, it was found that, there is every likelihood of depletion of water, if the petitioners' units are renewed with the licences. 12. However, learned Senior Counsel for the petitioners submitted that, petitioners have closed the second bore well constructed by them, evident from the photographs produced, and it is also stated that, the bore well could not be closed in the presence of the officials, since the people in the locality did not permit the bore well to be closed down. So also, it is pointed out that, petitioners are prepared to abide by the quantity of water that can be drawn as is permitted by the Pollution Control Board to the extent of 1700 litres and 300 litres, per day, respectively. However, learned counsel appearing for the Panchayat and the learned Senior Counsel for the 3rd respondent submitted that, the bore well is not de-commissioned and the manner in which the bore well is closed shows that the petitioners may be able to re-use the same. 13. That apart, it is submitted by learned Standing Counsel for the Panchayat that petitioners have not so far removed the illegal construction carried out to the already existing building, and therefore, unless and until the defects are rectified by the petitioners to the satisfaction of the Panchayat, the action now taken by the Panchayat declining renewal of licence to the petitioners is in order. It is also pointed out that, Ext.P43 is an appealable order, and therefore, petitioners have not made out any case justifying interference of this Court exercising the power of judicial review under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
